title: Microsoft Adds Report Meeting Feature to Teams to Combat AI Identity Impersonation and Deepfakes

content_html:
Microsoft has confirmed that it will launch a new "Report a Concern" feature for Microsoft Teams in August 2026, allowing participants to directly report phishing, identity theft, fraud, social engineering, and other suspicious activities during meetings. This will enable enterprise security teams to intervene quickly and investigate, helping to address the growing risks of AI-driven cyber fraud.

Microsoft stated that with the widespread adoption of generative AI technology, the barriers for attackers to use AI to collect corporate public information, generate deepfakes of participants, clone voices, or replicate facial features continue to decrease. Microsoft's previous research indicated that AI-driven fraud attacks have rapidly spread globally, with a large number of activities originating from China and Europe, and warned that related threats in markets such as Germany are continuously increasing.

The new feature allows users to submit security reports within Teams meetings or meeting chats. Relevant meeting metadata and limited context information will be recorded and synchronized to the Microsoft Defender portal and Teams Admin Center, enabling organizational administrators and security teams to analyze potential security incidents such as deepfakes and identity theft. Microsoft emphasized that this data is mainly provided to enterprise administrators for internal investigations and will not be automatically sent to Microsoft.

In addition to the new reporting mechanism, Microsoft also announced enhanced management of AI meeting bots. In the future, Teams will be able to identify external AI bots and display their identity and permissions to meeting organizers, helping administrators control the actions that bots can perform, preventing unauthorized AI assistants from entering meetings, thus further enhancing meeting security and privacy protection.

content_html_zh:
微软确认将于 2026 年 8 月为 Microsoft Teams 推出新的“报告问题”功能，允许参与者在会议期间直接报告网络钓鱼、身份盗窃、欺诈、社交工程和其他可疑活动。 这将使企业安全团队能够快速干预和调查，帮助解决人工智能驱动的网络欺诈日益增长的风险。

微软表示，随着生成式人工智能技术的广泛采用，攻击者利用人工智能收集企业公共信息、生成参与者的深度伪造品、克隆声音或复制面部特征的障碍不断减少。 微软此前的研究表明，人工智能驱动的欺诈攻击已在全球范围内迅速蔓延，其中大量活动源自中国和欧洲，并警告德国等市场的相关威胁正在不断增加。

新功能允许用户在 Teams 会议或会议聊天中提交安全报告。 相关会议元数据和有限的上下文信息将被记录并同步到 Microsoft Defender 门户和 Teams 管理中心，使组织管理员和安全团队能够分析潜在的安全事件，例如深度伪造和身份盗窃。 微软强调，这些数据主要提供给企业管理员用于内部调查，不会自动发送给微软。

除了新的报告机制外，微软还宣布加强对人工智能会议机器人的管理。 未来，Teams将能够识别外部AI机器人，并向会议组织者展示其身份和权限，帮助管理员控制机器人可以执行的操作，防止未经授权的AI助手进入会议，从而进一步增强会议安全和隐私保护。
